FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Bitumen, 
Tar and Related Products Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Product 
Division Council. 


Cracking in pavements generally occurs when a stress is built up in a surface layer that exceeds the tensile or shear 
strength of the pavement causing a fissure or crack to open. Crack sealing and crack filling are the two methods 
generally used to repair cracks in pavement surfaces. The main purposes of crack sealing and filling are: 


a) To prevent the intrusion of water through the cracks into the underlying layers of the pavement structure 
which further weakens the pavement. Many distresses are related to water infiltration. If water is kept out 
of the pavement system, there is a good chance distresses will not develop. 


b) To prevent incompressible materials from entering the cracks as they may cause deterioration when the 
pavement expands and contracts with temperature changes. 


Crack sealing is an important maintenance procedure of the pavements having proper drainage system. It is 
proficient where working cracks are subject to expansion and contraction by using specially prepared hot-poured 
sealant. Crack sealing may be considered as a permanent crack treatment procedure. Depending upon the material 
used, the condition of the pavement and the techniques used when applying crack sealant, the expected life is 
generally three to eight years. 


Crack filling is usually done on non-working cracks with bitumen emulsion or liquid bitumen (hot) to reduce 
water infiltration and to reinforce the adjacent pavement. It is usually considered as a temporary crack treatment 
procedure. Such fillers are only effective as long as the pavement remains stationary, both longitudinally and 
vertically. Once expansion and contraction or excessive vertical movement occurs, the effectiveness of filler may 
be lost and therefore cracks must be refilled. The severity level of the climate in a particular area is the main 
deciding factor for the crack treatment process. 


Many types of asphalt crack sealing materials are available in the market and certain important properties of cracks 
sealing include good bonding /adhesion; flexibility and elasticity; ease of application; resistance to softening; 
resistance to cracking; resistance to aging and weathering and compatibility. 


In preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been derived from Asphalt Institute publications. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17124 : 2019 


Indian Standard 
CRACK SEALANTS — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements, methods 
of sampling and tests for crack sealants used for 
filling or sealing cracks in asphalt/cement concrete 
pavements. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision 
and parties to agreement based on the standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the 
most recent editions of the standards indicated below:

3 TYPES 


The crack sealants shall be of following two types: 


a) Type I — The crack sealant used to seal cracks of 
15 mm width (Max) in asphalt/concrete pavements. 
This crack sealant is capable of maintaining an 
effective seal in moderate climates. 


b) Type II — The crack sealant used to seal cracks 
wider than 15 mm in asphalt/concrete pavements. 
This crack sealant is capable of maintaining an 
effective seal in all climates. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 The crack sealant shall be composed of a mixture 
of materials which forms a resilient and adhesive 
compound capable of effectively sealing joints and 
cracks in concrete and asphaltic pavement against the 
infiltration of moisture and foreign material throughout 
repeated cycles of expansion and contraction with 
temperature changes, and that will not, at ambient 
temperatures, flow from the joint or be picked up by 
vehicle tyres. 


4.2 The filling/sealing material shall be capable of being 
brought to a uniform pouring consistency suitable for 
completely filling the joints without the inclusion of 
large air holes or discontinuities and without damage 
to the pavement material. It shall remain relatively 
unchanged in application characteristics for at least 
6 hours at the recommended application temperature in 
the field. 


4.3 Recommended filling/sealing materials are given in 


Table 1.

4.4 Maximum Heating Temperature 


The maximum heating temperature is the highest 
temperature to which a crack sealant can be heated 
and still conforms to all the requirements specified 
in the standard. The maximum heating temperature 
shall be set forth by the manufacturer. It shall be 11°C 
higher than the maximum application temperature. 
However, for the purpose of testing, the application 
temperature shall be same as the maximum heating 
temperature. 


4.5 The crack sealant shall comply with the requirements 
given in Table 2 when tested as prescribed in col 5 of 
Table 2. 


5 PACKING AND MARKING 


5.1 Packing 


Crack sealant shall be delivered in the manufacturer’s 
original containers. 


5.2 Marking 


5.2.1 Each container of Crack sealant shall be legibly 
and indelibly marked with the following: 


a) Name of the manufacturer and the trade name of 
the sealant; 

b) The manufacturer’s batch, or lot number; 

c) IS No. and type of sealant; and 

d) Maximum application temperature and maximum 
heating temperature. 


5.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The material may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1.1 The product(s) conforming to the requirements 
of this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and 
Regulations framed thereunder, and the products may 
be marked with the standard mark. 


6 SAMPLING 


All samplings shall be carried out in accordance to 
IS 1201.

ANNEX A 
[ Table 2, Sl. No. (iv) ] 
DETERMINATION OF ELASTIC RECOVERY 


A-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The elastic recovery of crack sealants is evaluated 
by comparing recovery of thread after conditioning 
for 1 hat specified temperature and the specimen 
is elongated up to 10 cm deformation in a ductility 
machine. This is intended to assess degree of bitumen 
modification by Elastomeric additives. The cross 
section of the thread shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 


i A 
i 27] 
1 f : 
a 


A-36.5+0.1 mm 
B-30.0+0.1 mm 
C-17.0+0.1 mm 
D-10.0+0.1 mm 
E-10.0+ 


0.1 mm 


Fic. 1 DESIGN OF MOULD FOR ELASTIC RECOVERY 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 Ductility Machine and Moulds — As per 
IS 1208 and Fig. 1. 


A-2.2 Thermometer — Any standard thermometer 
(ASTM 63°C) of equivalent range and accuracy shall 
be used. 


A-2.3 Scissors — Any type of conventional scissors 
capable of cutting modified bitumen at the test 
temperature. 


A 2.4 Scale — Any transparent scale of measuring up 
to 25 cm with + 1 mm accuracy. 


A-3 PROCEDURE 


A-3.1 Prepare the test specimens in a set of three 
moulds as per dimensions given in Fig. 1 and condition 
as prescribed in test method of IS 1208. Elongate the 
test specimen at the specified rate to a deformation of 
10 cm at arate of 5 + 0.25 cm/min and immediately cut 
the test specimen into two halves at the mid-point using 
the scissors. Keep the test specimen in the water bath in 
an undisturbed condition for | h before testing. 


A-3.2 After 1 h time period, move the elongated half 
of the test specimen back into position near the fixed 
half of the test specimen so the two pieces of modified 
bitumen just touch. Record the length of the recombined 
specimen as X. 


A-4 REPORT 


Calculate the percent/elastic recovery by the following 
procedure: 


: 10-X 
Elastic recovery, percent = m x100 
Where, 


X = length, in cm, of recombined specimen.
